input.rationale: Started from the (Fe,Cr)VO4 region, where V is about 0.5. XRD at 107 and 25 showed the same main phase, with its dominant peak at Q≈2.78. Swapping Fe for Cr at constant V raised the photocurrent from 3.8e-7 A (107) to 6.1e-7 A (25). Following that trend to 68 (Cr 0.375, Fe 0.168, V 0.456) gave 1.14e-6 A, the highest measured.

content.text:
I've submitted index 68 (Cr 0.375, Fe 0.168, V 0.456) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 1.14 µA. I can't tell how close that is to the library's true best, since the other 198 compositions went unmeasured.

With only three merit measurements, I started where I expected a known photoanode material: iron vanadate (FeVO4) with some Cr in place of Fe, around 50% V. I then moved in the direction that improved photocurrent:

| Index | Cr / Fe / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | 0.138 / 0.347 / 0.515 | 0.38 µA |
| 25 | 0.258 / 0.242 / 0.500 | 0.61 µA |
| 68 | 0.375 / 0.168 / 0.456 | 1.14 µA |

- **Trend:** photocurrent rose steadily as Cr replaced Fe, so the optimum may lie at even higher Cr. Index 189 (Cr 0.367, Fe 0.136, V 0.496) would be the next one to test.
- **XRD:** I used 3 of the 5 scans. Indices 107 and 25 showed the same main crystal phase. The V-rich index 2 also had peaks consistent with a separate V2O5 phase, so I didn't measure that region's photocurrent.
